analyst.summary: RIL's Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) posted record segment EBITDA in both O2C (Rs 17,010 crore, GRM-driven) and Jio (Rs 20,865 crore, tariff/ARPU-driven), but reported net profit fell 22.4% YoY to Rs 20,946 crore purely because Q1 FY26 contained a one-off Asian Paints stake-sale gain -- core operations are not deteriorating. Retail is the one segment with a genuine, company-acknowledged trend problem: EBITDA fell 1.1% YoY as JioMart's quick-commerce expansion trades margin for share against loss-making rivals. Balance sheet leverage is stable (net debt ~Rs 1.40 lakh crore, D/E 0.45, interest cover 6.6x, no red flags), but free cash flow remains slightly negative as a second capex cycle (the Rs 75,000 crore Jamnagar New Energy giga-complex) layers onto a telecom capex cycle that has only just peaked. The single biggest near-term swing factor is the Jio Platforms IPO (DRHP filed, H2 2026 listing guided, implied $133-180bn valuation) -- our own conservative sum-of-the-parts estimate puts current RIL equity value roughly in line with the current market cap (~Rs 17.5-18.0 lakh crore), meaning the stock is neither obviously cheap nor obviously expensive on fundamentals, with the IPO print as the catalyst that could move it materially either way. Given no balance-sheet/governance breaks and record core-segment EBITDA, this review calls Hold over the quant model's Sell, but flags genuine analytical tension given mediocre ROE/ROCE, still-negative FCF, and a structurally challenged O2C petrochemical sub-segment.
